purpose: Distinguish an independently published 2000 Tucson congregational chronology from missing sermon manuscripts, and exclude a different congregation's misleading 2015 Temple Times title.

first_party_historical_context.organization: Kol Ami Synagogue (Tucson); successor institutional history of Temple Emanu-El
first_party_historical_context.observation: Official detailed Temple history identifies 90th-anniversary celebrations in March 2000, including a Heritage Shabbat held at the Stone Avenue Temple on March 11 and a separate March 17 recognition of Joan and Donald Diamond.
first_party_historical_context.event_relation_to_target_sermon: Historical 2000-era congregation activities; not the Yom Kippur 5761 sermon, not a manuscript or written service transcript.

historical_public_museum_context.observation: A 2010 centennial exhibit at the Jewish History Museum, in the original Stone Avenue Temple building, reportedly displayed an early Temple Emanu-El newsletter among other historical materials.
historical_public_museum_context.evidence_type: contemporaneous secondary description of publicly exhibited early historical document
historical_public_museum_context.collection_scope_limit: The reported exhibit concerns early institutional heritage, not authenticated writings from 2000, 2001, or 2015.

same_title_false_positive.exclusion_basis: 2015 PDF mastheads identify Temple Beth Shalom (Established 1953; United Synagogue of Conservative Judaism), whereas authenticated Tucson Temple Times mastheads identify Temple Emanu-El at 225 N Country Club Road. The collections have different ShulCloud IDs and publishers.

additional_recheck.status: Public Rabbi Sam Cohon blog homepage verified; visible 2018–2021 era posts and tags are not evidence that either requested original 2000/2001/2015 Temple manuscript is hosted there.
additional_recheck.hv009_detail_result: Cache miss in web browser, including a fresh publisher-index link traversal
